units.function: A 7,771-line Tool Access orchestration service covering applications, connections, OAuth/DCR/refresh, secrets, grants, installs, profiles, catalogs, runtime slots, policy/approval projections, invocation evidence, token exchange and gallery/example workflows.
units.dependencyDirection: Depends directly on most Tool Access database tables, secrets, policy, runtime supervision, shared provider schemas and provider-specific Google Sheets/Notion behavior; routes and gateway callers depend on it. This is a broad server application service rather than a vendor-neutral port or bounded connector module.
units.keyDataModels: ToolApplication, ToolConnection, ConnectionGrant, ConnectionInstall, OAuthState, CatalogEntry, Profile/Entry/Binding, Policy/TrustRule, RuntimeSlot, Invocation, ActionRequest, ToolCallEvent, TokenIssuance and provider-specific connection configuration.
units.lifecycle: Creates/configures applications and connections, stores secret references, discovers/refreshes catalogs, computes effective profiles and policies, runs health/runtime operations, coordinates OAuth authorization and refresh leases, mints short-lived upstream tokens, pauses Tool calls for approval and projects audit/attention state.
units.testAssessment: The complete 6,996-line integration suite is unusually broad: route permissions, tenant hiding, OAuth actor/session binding, PKCE/DCR, secret-backed storage, database refresh leases, approval signatures, gallery transaction rollback, deletion races, runtime controls, viewer regression and value-free audit records. Local focused execution passed 7 pure tests while 118 database-backed cases were skipped, so no full local pass is claimed. Important missing or codified-bad cases remain: refresh-secret rotation before losing CAS, external token minted before nontransactional audit/state writes, returned scope/actual expiry enforcement, concurrent rate-limit consumption, uninstall revocation, multi-instance DCR, callback retry after state consumption, catalog removal, scale bounds, archive authority cleanup and fail-open unknown-mutation classification.
units.designRationale: Centralize a complete governed Tool/MCP product slice quickly while using secret references, policy profiles, approval requests, runtime health and audit projections to make external Tool use operationally manageable.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS needs the same end-to-end concerns, but as independently owned Connector, Authorization, Credential Broker, Approval/Evidence and Runtime bounded contexts with accountable-human and data-contract invariants.
units.companyOsFit: REFERENCE the lifecycle coverage, direct/redirect SSRF guard, OAuth actor/session binding, database refresh lease, strict DCR response validation, secret-free attestation/audit, tenant-hiding reads, board-test actor separation, gallery transaction and NO ACTION race defense. Reimplement behind Company OS ports with transactional outbox/idempotency, atomic rate-limit claims, exact returned-scope/expiry checks, fail-closed risk classification, explicit install revocation, bounded projections and provider logic isolated in connectors.
units.responsibilityConflict: The service can attribute fixture smoke activity to the first real Agent, derives accountable user mainly from mutable run snapshots rather than a versioned ResponsibilityContract, permits incomplete approval/invocation terminal states, and stores operational/audit evidence across duplicate tables without one immutable chain binding goal, work, permissions, data contract, human decision, action digest, evidence and result.

units.function: Large embedded-PostgreSQL integration and route test suite for the Tool Access orchestration boundary.
units.dependencyDirection: Exercises Express routes, database migrations/schema, Tool Access/Policy/Gateway services, secret storage and runtime collaborators; it is downstream verification rather than production ownership.
units.keyDataModels: Applications, connections, OAuth state/tokens, grants, installs, profiles, policies, catalogs, invocations, action requests, runtime slots, activity/audit records and user/Agent authorization contexts.
units.lifecycle: Builds isolated companies/users/Agents/runs and external HTTP fixtures, drives connection/OAuth/profile/policy/approval/runtime workflows, injects selected failures and asserts database state, response visibility and audit redaction.
units.testAssessment: Behavioral breadth and security regression coverage are strong, including genuine two-service refresh concurrency, transaction rollback and database FK race tests. It nevertheless skips key atomicity/failure windows and explicitly accepts unsafe product semantics such as non-Notion move_pages classified read and cross-tenant Google spreadsheet identifiers returned in conflict errors. Many scale/concurrency/cleanup invariants are absent. Direct local execution passed only the 7 non-database tests and skipped 118 database-backed tests because the current environment lacked test database support.
units.designRationale: Use one end-to-end suite to keep a rapidly growing cross-table Tool Access feature coherent across HTTP, services, database and external-provider boundaries.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS needs executable responsibility, credential, approval and connector compatibility contracts that detect partial failures and unsafe authority transitions, not only happy-path feature regressions.
units.companyOsFit: ADAPT the embedded-database fixture style, real HTTP OAuth fixtures, tenant/viewer matrices, database-race tests, secret-value absence assertions and failure injection. Split by bounded context and add property/concurrency/crash recovery, uninstall/archive revocation, scope/expiry, outbox, large-tenant and ResponsibilityContract invariants.
units.responsibilityConflict: Several assertions freeze Paperclip-specific authority semantics that Company OS must reject; copying the suite unchanged would make unsafe classification, identifier disclosure and incomplete responsibility state look normative.

units.function: Express HTTP surface for Agent token/OAuth flows and board-facing Tool gallery, connection, grant, install, test-call, catalog, profile, runtime, policy, trust-rule, stdio-template, import and policy-test operations.
units.dependencyDirection: Depends on Express, shared request schemas, board/company authorization, access decisions, Tool Access/Policy/Gateway services and database Agent/company queries; it exposes a Paperclip-specific API rather than a stable external Company OS contract.
units.keyDataModels: Authenticated board or Agent actor, company membership/permission, run id, connection/application/profile/policy identifiers, gateway reason codes and activity-log entries.
units.lifecycle: Validates most request bodies, resolves resource ownership, applies one of several authorization helpers, delegates mutation/query to services, writes activity records and renders JSON, redirect or structured gateway errors.
units.testAssessment: The linked integration suite covers viewer denial, cross-company 404 hiding, OAuth callback actor/session checks, runtime permission, test-call assignment rights and many mutation paths. Missing route-level coverage includes granular permission consistency, bounded list inputs, manual grant-body element validation, viewer-triggered audit writes, structured error-code stability and atomic mutation/activity logging.
units.designRationale: Offer the native Paperclip board and Agent runtime a single REST surface while reusing service-layer orchestration and existing membership/access helpers.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS requires an independently versioned API with stable codes, narrow command/query contracts and explicit permissions for connection, profile, policy, approval, runtime and audit authority changes.
units.companyOsFit: REFERENCE tenant-hiding resource reads, authenticated run/header binding, exact tasks:assign check for board test calls, real-user versus selected-Agent attribution and strict tools:admin/runtime permissions. Replace broad non-viewer mutation access with purpose-specific capabilities and ResponsibilityContract checks; validate every input through schemas, bound pagination and emit structured codes plus transactional/outbox audit evidence.
units.responsibilityConflict: Any active non-viewer may mutate applications, connections, Profiles, Policies and Trust Rules, while MCP import preview and policy test can let viewers create activity/audit effects. Activity writes occur after mutations, and most failures are English strings rather than stable codes. These semantics are too broad and brittle for Company OS human accountability.
